item.title: British adventurer returns home after 28-year journey around the world
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby returns to his mother’s home in Hull after completing a 28-year, 50,000-kilometre journey from Chile.

item.title: British government sets out tougher rules for migrants looking to settle in the UK
item.description: British PM Andy Burnham said the UK had "lost control of immigration" following Brexit. "This Home Secretary is gripping this problem, and she has my full support in doing so."

item.title: Britain’s 'oldest cars' hit the road for annual London to Brighton run
item.description: The UK celebrates 140 years of the motor car as pre-1905 vehicles parade through London's historic streets before heading to Brighton.

item.title: Ukraine says hopes of 'progress toward peace' knocked by attack on aid distribution centre
item.description: Zelenskyy said the Zaporizhzhia attack showed Russia was "sending an entirely opposite signal" and that it was "counting on more killings."

item.title: Recent virus outbreaks show urgent need to complete pandemic treaty, says WHO chief
item.description: The WHO chief said recent outbreaks of Ebola and hantavirus show why countries must finalise the agreement without delay.

item.title: Climber rescued after being abandoned at 2,600 metres in Austrian Alps
item.description: Gerhard Kremser, the district manager of the Pongau Mountain Rescue Service, said the man likely would not have survived another night on the mountain due to the conditions.

item.title: Inside Milipol Qatar, where drones and robots take on security and emergency response roles
item.description: From a drone carrying traffic lights to a remotely operated robot, exhibitors at Milipol Qatar demonstrate equipment designed for emergency response, surveillance and work in dangerous places.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 2nd, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Watch: Unseen images of drone sinking Greek tanker off Bulgarian coast
item.description: Russia is suspected of being behind a recent wave of attacks targeting commercial vessels in the Black Sea.

item.title: Ebola kills over 5,300 in fastest-growing outbreak on record
item.description: The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, has infected more than 10,000 people since May and has spread to Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.

item.title: Supermarket hacks across Europe: why are fridges connected to the internet?
item.description: As hackers target supermarket cooling systems across Europe, new research finds nearly 13,000 refrigeration controls openly reachable online in 99 countries, from supermarkets to hospitals and farms, many running outdated software.

item.title: Ukraine’s ‘Stargate’ drone carries wounded troops from frontline
item.description: Ukraine’s Skyfall says its Stargate drone has evacuated two wounded soldiers from the front line, flying 15 km each way at up to 105 km/h.

item.title: Polish PM Donald Tusk urges president to confirm judges amid constitutional crisis
item.description: Polish PM Tusk accused Karol Nawrocki of "opting for a forceful confrontation" as he called on him to recognise the judges "lawfully elected by the Sejm."

item.title: Ukraine to channel up to €1bn in EU loans into joint defence projects
item.description: Ukraine is set to move up to €1bn of its EU loan into the Ukraine Support Instrument to integrate its defence industry with its European partners. The move is part of a Defence Industrial Pact that should remove regulatory hurdles for industrial cooperation and to encourage member states to destock.

item.title: Former Greek PM Papandreou calls for protection of EU prosecutors
item.description: Former Greek Prime Minister George Papandreou calls in an guest article for Euronews for stronger safeguards to protect the independence of the European Public Prosecutor's Office, following recent warnings from its outgoing chief, Laura Kövesi, about political pressure to investigations in Greece.

item.title: Wizz Air flight from London to Sofia diverts after 'bomb threat'
item.description: "The aircraft diverted and landed safely at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport in accordance with the relevant security protocols and procedures," the airline said in a statement shared with Euronews.

item.title: Fridges stand empty in Belgian supermarkets after cyberattack
item.description: Supermarkets in several European countries have reported cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems, causing food to spoil and forcing some stores to close off their fridges and freezers.

item.title: Europe sees disasters coming. Can it act in time?
item.description: Europe is turning vast climate data into intelligence, using GIS and AI to guide emergency responses, prevent disasters and protect the economy.

item.title: What did people eat and drink 4,000 years ago? New finds shed light on life in Mesopotamia
item.description: Archaeologists working at Tell Muhammad in Baghdad have uncovered new evidence of daily life in ancient Mesopotamia, including possible bread and beer production facilities. The site dates mainly to the era of Hammurabi, around 2000 to 1600 BC.

item.title: Humanoid robots climb China’s Mount Tai in unusual challenge
item.description: China's Mount Tai hosts a robot challenge, with nearly 90 teams tackling 3,100 steps and a 600-metre climb on an ancient mountain path.

item.title: UK and Germany to jointly develop military AI in 2027
item.description: Government and industry figures will meet next spring to shape the plan, though no specific systems or budgets have been named so far.

item.title: US midterm elections 2026: What are they and when will we know the results?
item.description: Americans head to the polls on 3 November for midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the next two years.

item.title: Brussels still 'traumatised' by Brexit, EU foreign policy chief warns
item.description: The EU and UK are meeting for a summit on November 20th where both sides agree on the need for greater cooperation, but differences remain on how to get there.

item.title: 28 years and 50,000 kilometres: British adventurer Karl Bushby arrives home after epic trek
item.description: A crowd of up to 1,000 people cheered as the former British paratrooper arrived back in Hull, England, after his 50,000-kilometre journey.

item.title: Taliban voices 'serious concern' over US plans to deport Afghans via Pakistan
item.description: Advocacy groups have warned that the removal of former allies and their families could endanger their lives.

item.title: Skeleton puppets and zombies fill New York’s Halloween parade
item.description: Skeleton puppets, zombies and film characters take over Greenwich Village. Thousands join the 53rd New York Halloween parade, dancing through Manhattan.

item.title: Ukraine needs help this winter, says UN goodwill ambassador and actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau
item.description: Ukraine needs help this winter, says UN goodwill ambassador and actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau

item.title: Portugal house prices hit new record as October sees 7.5% annual rise
item.description: House prices in Portugal rose 7.5% in October compared with the same period last year. The price per square metre in Lisbon exceeds six thousand euros.

item.title: Schools closed and roads flooded as new wave of severe weather hits Greek islands
item.description: Although the intense weather phenomena eased during the morning hours, emergency services remain on high alert, as further rain and thunderstorms cannot be ruled out during the day.

item.title: Iran says it can reopen Hormuz in two days if US meets conditions
item.description: Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the timeline shortened from the seven days first proposed in September was “another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach” but that “everything depends” on Washington.

item.title: Prague, Kraków and Istanbul: These are the best European cities for solo travellers
item.description: A new ranking for solo travel has evaluated the most visited European cities by looking at things like accommodation costs and the perception of safety.

item.title: Apple's new CEO faces earnings test as rising chip costs cloud outlook
item.description: Investors want clarity on Christmas sales, rising memory costs and Apple's AI plans as John Ternus prepares to lead his first earnings call since taking over from Tim Cook.

item.title: From Christmas magic to snowy escapes: 10 of Europe’s best winter travel destinations
item.description: Europe has a wealth of diverse destinations to visit during winter, whether you are looking for snowy escapes, coastal breaks or historic journeys.

item.title: Limited school protests resume in some cities in France as holiday ends
item.description: The government has announced measures, including changing the university admissions process, ensuring more teachers and capping the number of pupils per class.

item.title: Argentina courts AI data centres with no regulation and tax breaks
item.description: Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, is courting AI data centre investment in Patagonia, promising light regulation and tax breaks.

item.title: UK pulls the plug on analogue phones in January and the rest of Europe is next
item.description: Businesses face soaring costs and disrupted services if they delay, as Brussels pushes for copper networks to be retired across the EU by 2035.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 2nd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Canadian minister stops short of endorsing EU carbon tax as energy alliance deepens
item.description: The Canadian climate Minister's reluctance to openly commit to cooperation with the EU on its climate policy stems from the fact that Ottawa is effectively seeking an exemption from the bloc's carbon border tax, according to a December 2025 internal document seen by Euronews.

item.title: Bolivia declares national emergency over El Niño as drought hits over 78,000 families
item.description: Drought is already affecting more than 78,000 families in seven regions of the country.

item.title: Cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe, Belgium launches investigation
item.description: A number of incidents have taken place affecting supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Netherlands, Estonia, Luxembourg, Finland and Ireland, with fridge and freezer temperatures turned up, spoiling food.

item.title: Oil slides on Hormuz deal hopes but Trump keeps Iran strikes on the table
item.description: Oil prices fell on Monday morning as talks in Qatar revived hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but US President Donald Trump kept the threat of fresh strikes alive and Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly urged him to hit Iran straight after Tuesday's midterm elections.

item.title: Russia resumes attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region after truce ends, Kyiv says
item.description: The ceasefire enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and for hundreds of stranded citizens to leave.

item.title: Ryanair eyes cost cuts as it faces a €2 billion rise in its fuel bill next year
item.description: One of Europe's biggest airlines saw its first-half profit fall 15% as higher fuel costs and lower fares outweighed passenger growth.

item.title: Prada champions the human touch and not AI slop for their new Christmas campaign
item.description: Prada's new advertising feels like a direct response to those still indulging in a tech that is threatening human creativity and livelihoods. Their ‘Drawing Prada: Animated By Hand’ campaign shows that the "not-made-by-AI" approach has become a major selling point.

item.title: Can the EU’s energy solutions lower your bills? Take our poll
item.description: EU energy ministers want to shield households and businesses from a harsh winter pricing, as the massive geopolitical shock in the Middle East has sent European gas prices surging past a four-year high of €97 per megawatt-hour.

item.title: Dutch MP proposes law banning 'harmful addictive design features' on all digital platforms
item.description: MP Barbara Kathmann tabled a proposal in the Dutch Parliament to end addictive design features such as endless scrolling, autoplay and manipulative algorithms for all online services including social media, gaming, dating apps and streaming platforms.

item.title: Mbappé’s ‘Chinese dictator’ comment: How do Chinese people react?
item.description: Kylian Mbappé has apologised after remarks about a meme depicting him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong sparked backlash in China. At least three Chinese companies have ended brand deals with the football star, while the controversy has drawn a response from China's Foreign Ministry.

item.title: German MPs and ministers warned iPhones have been targeted by spyware
item.description: Those affected have been told to treat their phones as compromised, but it is not yet known who is behind the attack or how many people were hit.

item.title: Paris riots: France investigates after petrol bomb sets officer on fire
item.description: France has opened an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at police during protests over the rising cost of living in Paris.

item.title: Serbia remembers 16 victims of Novi Sad railway station collapse
item.description: Serbia marks two years since the Novi Sad station collapse, as students in power vow justice for the 16 victims and accountability for alleged corruption.
